body.statement: For every \(m\geq1\): if \(K=2\), then \(C\sim C'\) if and only if \(C'=C\) or \(C'=C^\top\); if \(K\geq3\), then \(C\sim C'\) if and only if \(C'=C\) or \(\{C,C'\}=\{C_+,C_-\}\). Whenever \(C\not\sim C'\), one has \(d(C,C')\leq3\).
body.justification: The theorem gives the complete outcome-alphabet phase change in exact weak-null symmetry and a uniform constructive certificate for every nonequivalence.
body.gap: The closest results are the i.i.d. finite-support criterion of \cite{DutzZhang2026} and the asymptotic fixed-population theorem of \cite{WuDing2021}; neither classifies the all-schedule hypergeometric kernel.
body.consumer: DeclareDesign's balanced \(250\)-of-\(500\) binary reply audit can use this theorem to state exactly which histogram transformations, rather than which sharp-null imputations, are justified by the weak average-effect null.
body.proof_tex:
We first prove the positive equivalences.  Equality \(C\sim C\) is immediate from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}equivalence}\).  If \(K=2\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}weak\text{-}null}\) reduces to
\[
 R_{10}-R_{01}=0,
\]
so every legal binary response table satisfies \(R=R^\top\).  Complementing a balanced assignment and simultaneously interchanging the two coordinates of every response type gives the coefficient identity
\[
 W_R(h,g)=W_{R^\top}(g,h).                              \tag{1}
\]
This is a bijection because an assignment and its complement both have \(m\) treated units.  Since \(R=R^\top\), (1) and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}randomization\text{-}kernel}\) prove \(C\sim C^\top\) in the binary case.  For every \(K\geq3\), Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}endpoint\text{-}saturation}\) gives equal assignment counts for \(C_+\) and \(C_-\) under every legal table, and hence \(C_+\sim C_-\).

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}transpose\text{-}reduction}\) proves that no equivalence class can contain anything other than a profile and its transpose.  It remains to decide which nontrivial transpose pairs survive when \(K\geq3\), and to control the number of heterogeneous units in a separator.  Fix \(C=(h,g)\ne C^\top\), put \(r=h+g\), and first suppose that the support
\[
 S=\{a\in\mathcal A_K:r_a>0\}
\]
contains an interior point.  On \(S\), join every distinct pair except possibly \(\{0,L\}\).  This graph is connected because an interior vertex joins both endpoints.  If
\[
 h_a g_b-g_a h_b=0                                      \tag{2}
\]
on every edge, then \(g=r-h\) turns (2) into \(h_a/r_a=h_b/r_b\).  Connectivity makes this ratio constant on \(S\), and the identities \(\sum_a h_a=m\) and \(\sum_a r_a=2m\) make the constant \(1/2\).  That would give \(h=g\), contrary to the choice of \(C\).  Hence there are \(a<b\) with \(\{a,b\}\ne\{0,L\}\) for which (2) is nonzero.

For such \(a,b\), choose \(u,v\in\mathcal A_K\) by
\[
 (u,v)=
 \begin{cases}
 (b-a,0),&a>0,\\
 (b+1,1),&a=0.
 \end{cases}                                             \tag{3}
\]
In the second line \(b<L\), so all four values lie in the alphabet.  In both lines \(a+u=v+b\), and both response types below are heterogeneous.  Define
\[
 R_2=D_{r-e_a-e_b}+E_{av}+E_{ub}.                        \tag{4}
\]
Its mass is \(2m\), its filler is nonnegative because \(r_a,r_b>0\), and the sum of its two nonzero effects is \((a-v)+(u-b)=0\).  Thus (4) is legal by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}weak\text{-}null}\).  Directly checking the two choices in (3) shows that, among the four allocations of the special units, only treating the \((a,v)\) unit and controlling the \((u,b)\) unit adds the pooled histogram \(e_a+e_b\) required on top of the diagonal filler.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}assignment\text{-}count}\) therefore gives
\[
 W_{R_2}(C)=Q_r(h)\frac{h_a g_b}{r_a r_b},\qquad
 W_{R_2}(C^\top)=Q_r(h)\frac{g_a h_b}{r_a r_b}.          \tag{5}
\]
The denominator is positive, and (2) says the two counts in (5) differ.  Thus every nontrivial transpose whose pooled histogram has interior support has a legal separator with two heterogeneous units.

It remains to consider profiles supported on \(\{0,L\}\).  Write
\[
 h_0=m-i,\quad h_L=i,\qquad g_0=m-j,\quad g_L=j,\qquad i\ne j. \tag{6}
\]
If only one endpoint were supported, the two arm-size constraints would force \(h=g\), so the relevant pooled endpoint counts are positive.  Consider
\[
 R'_2=D_{r-e_0-e_L}+E_{L,1}+E_{0,L-1}.                  \tag{7}
\]
Here \(L\geq2\).  The two effects in (7) are \(L-1\) and \(-(L-1)\), so the table is legal and has two heterogeneous units.  Because both special control outcomes are interior, an endpoint-only profile is possible only when both special units are treated.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{R'_2}(C)-W_{R'_2}(C^\top)
 &=\frac{Q_r(h)}{r_0r_L}\bigl(h_0h_L-g_0g_L\bigr)\\
 &=\frac{Q_r(h)}{r_0r_L}(i-j)(m-i-j).
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Thus (7) separates unless \(i+j=m\).

Suppose now \(i+j=m\).  Then \(r_0=r_L=m\), \(h_0=j\), \(g_0=i\).  If \(i=0\) or \(j=0\), the unordered pair \(\{C,C^\top\}\) is exactly \(\{C_+,C_-\}\), already shown equivalent.  Otherwise \(i,j>0\); since \(i\ne j\), necessarily \(m\geq3\).  Define the cubic table
\[
 R_3=D_{r-2e_0-e_L}+E_{L,0}+E_{0,1}+E_{0,L-1}.          \tag{9}
\]
Its diagonal filler is nonnegative, and its three heterogeneous effects sum to
\[
 L-1-(L-1)=0,
\]
so (9) is legal.  To produce an endpoint-only profile, the last two special units must be treated, because their control outcomes are interior.  The first special unit must also be treated: if it were controlled, the three special observations would contribute \(3e_0\), rather than the required \(2e_0+e_L\).  Thus exactly one special-unit allocation contributes, even when \(L=2\) and the last two response types coincide.  Binomial cancellation against \(Q_r(h)\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{R_3}(C)
 &=Q_r(h)\frac{h_0(h_0-1)h_L}{m^2(m-1)},\\
W_{R_3}(C^\top)
 &=Q_r(h)\frac{g_0(g_0-1)g_L}{m^2(m-1)},\\
W_{R_3}(C)-W_{R_3}(C^\top)
 &=Q_r(h)\frac{ij(j-i)}{m^2(m-1)}\ne0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
All divisions in (10) are valid because \(m\geq3\).  Equations (5), (8), and (10), together with Lemmas \(\mathrm{lem{:}transpose\text{-}reduction}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}endpoint\text{-}saturation}\), prove the asserted classification for \(K\geq3\).

Finally, the proof supplies the claimed separator map.  If two profiles have different pooled histograms, Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}diagonal\text{-}reduction}\) separates them with \(D_r\), for which \(q=0\).  If their pooled histograms agree but their diagonal coefficients differ, the same diagonal table separates them.  If those checks agree but the profiles are neither equal nor transposes, the constructive proof of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}transpose\text{-}reduction}\) supplies a symmetric switch with \(q=2\).  A remaining inequivalent transpose at \(K\geq3\) is separated by (4), (7), or (9), with \(q=2,2,3\), respectively.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}separator\text{-}size}\) therefore gives \(d(C,C')\leq3\) for every inequivalent pair.
